newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares steady, market seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares steady, market seen volatile.

text.p: Austrian shares closed steady on Friday after a quiet trading day dominated by the expiry of May ATX contracts, and traders said the market was likely to remain volatile until Tuesday's key Federal Reserve meeting.
"We're waiting to see what the Fed will do," said one, adding a decision to keep U.S. rates steady was expected to give the market a new boost.
The ATX index of 21 blue chips rose 1.99 points or 0.16 pct to close at 1,251.38, bringing its gain for the week to 0.83 percent. Among its constituents, 13 winners outnumbered eight losers.
Bank Austria led the day's gainers, rising 1.62 percent to 420 schillings after the bank on Thursday gave an upbeat outlook for its full-year earnings.
Elsewhere in the banking sector, preference shares of Creditanstalt, which in January fell under the control of Bank Austria, rose four schillings to 512 in heavy volume.

Brick maker Wienerberger continued to be in strong demand after the group on Thursday said it had sold a Vienna office and retail complex for three billion schillings in cash and liabilities. Its shares ended up 35 schillings at 2,365.05.
Engineering group VA Technologie led the day's losers, falling 2.11 percent to close at 1,983.20 schillings.
Outside the main ATX index, Austrian Airlines surged 3.77 percent to finish at 1,900 after its 42.85 percent owned Tyrolean Airways unit reported a strong set of first-quarter earnings.
On the Vienna futures and options exchange, the May ATX contract ended 7.3 points higher at 1,255.0, while the June contract was up 5.4 points at 1,250.0 on volume of 1,476 lots.
